title: The normalized rational Hom comparison for integral point sections
statement: Fix D, l and E as in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], with l different from the characteristic, and suppose its specified integral fibre functor is an equivalence. For integral constructible objects K and M there is an additive isomorphism from O_E[1/varpi_E] tensor over O_E with Hom(K,M) to Hom of their specified integral-rational fibres. It sends a tensor f to sfRationalCoefficientEquiv(a) times the integral-rational fibre of f, as a morphism in the ambient derived category. The localization and rational fibre are exactly those of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

proof.text: Every bounded $A$-complex with finitely generated cohomology is perfect. To verify the needed hypotheses explicitly, take a finitely generated module $N$. The Noetherian finite-free-resolution theorem gives $A^{r_1}\to A^{r_0}\to N\to0$. Its kernel $J\subset A^{r_0}$ is finitely generated, being the image of the first finite free term, and is torsion free because $A$ is a domain and $A^{r_0}$ is torsion free. The finite torsion-free DVR theorem makes $J$ finite free. Thus $0\to J\to A^{r_0}\to N\to0$ is a bounded finite-free resolution. The perfect-cohomology assembly theorem now gives a bounded finite-projective representative $Q$ for every $M\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$. The argument includes $N=0$ and does not impose finite Tor dimension on modules over $A_n$; those rings may be singular.

For the rational stage first check full faithfulness for the specified raw localization. Put $M=\Gamma(s,K)$, $N=\Gamma(s,K')$ for integral objects. The integral equivalence is $A$-linear: all its maps above are maps of $A$-modules and the section action is the canonical one. Thus it identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(K,K')$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(M,N)$ as $A$-modules. Both $M,N$ are perfect by step 6. Apply perfect RHom base change to $A\to E$ and the first argument $M$. Here $E=A[1/\pi]$ by the uniformizer localization theorem and is flat by localization flatness. Consequently taking $H^0$ of that base-change isomorphism, using flat-tensor exactness, gives the canonical bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(M,N)\otimes_AE\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(E)}(M\otimes_AE,N\otimes_AE)$. The identification $H^0(R\operatorname{Hom}(M,N))=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(M,N)$ is precisely the K-injective Hom-complex theorem applied on the one-object ringed site (and likewise for $E$). The base-change theorem specifies its map to be the scalar extension of the functor-induced Hom map; hence this bijection sends $f\otimes a$ to $a(f\otimes E)$, exactly the morphism map defining the rational fibre functor. The rationalization definition gives the left-hand Hom groups, so this proves full faithfulness without adjoining idempotents.

theorem pointRationalSectionsHom
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (hi : (pointIntegralFibre D l hl E).IsEquivalence)
    (K M : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E (Spec (.of D.k))) :
    ∃ e : (Localization.Away (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E) ⊗[
          Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E] (K ⟶ M)) ≃+
        ((pointIntegralRationalFibre D l hl E).obj K ⟶
          (pointIntegralRationalFibre D l hl E).obj M),
      ∀ (a : Localization.Away (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)) (f : K ⟶ M),
        (e (a ⊗ₜ[Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E] f)).hom =
          (sfRationalCoefficientEquiv l E a) •
            ((pointIntegralRationalFibre D l hl E).map f).hom
